task_summary: cell2location deconvolution of Visium mouse brain with sc_mouse_cortex reference

steps.title: Load and QC the single-cell reference
steps.description: Load /home/flavio/uv/squidpy/data/sc_mouse_cortex.h5ad (you download it first). Confirm the layer that holds raw integer counts (cell2location requires counts, not log values) and the label column (expected `cell_subclass`; `cell_class` for coarse labels). Report cells per type and drop types with fewer than 20 cells. Save `ref_celltype_counts.tsv` and a bar chart `ref_celltype_counts.png`. Also determine the protocol (Smart-seq vs 10x droplet) from per-cell total counts and metadata; this decides step 2.

steps.title: Fit the reference signature model
steps.description: If the reference is droplet (10x) data: apply cell2location.utils.filtering.filter_genes (cell_count_cutoff=5, cell_percentage_cutoff2=0.03, nonz_mean_cutoff=1.12) and train RegressionModel on counts (labels_key=cell_subclass, max_epochs=250), exporting inf_aver. If it is Smart-seq (expected for sc_mouse_cortex): follow the cell2location preprint (Kleshchevnikov 2020, Methods: 'Validation ... with region-specific scRNA-seq reference'), which states that the NB regression model is not suitable for Smart-seq and instead derives signatures as per-cluster average expression (cell2location.cluster_averages.compute_cluster_averages). Save `c2l_reference_signatures.tsv` and a signature QC figure (marker-gene heatmap) to root_result/root_figure.

steps.title: Fit the cell2location spatial model
steps.description: Use the Visium raw counts from `visium_hne.h5ad` (`adata.raw`), remove mitochondrial genes, and intersect genes with the signatures. Train Cell2location with priors taken from the preprint's mouse-brain Visium analysis: N_cells_per_location=8 (estimated from histology there; replaces the 30 I proposed earlier, which was a lymph-node value), detection_alpha=20; for a Smart-seq reference, set the technology-sensitivity prior detection_mean=1/20 as the paper did for its Smart-seq 4 reference. max_epochs=30000, full data, CPU, in the background. Export the q05 cell abundance per spot into obsm and save `visium_hne_c2l.h5ad` plus the model to root_data.

steps.title: Spot-level cell-type maps and summaries
steps.description: Convert abundances to per-spot fractions and add a dominant type plus its fraction per spot (flagging spots with dominant fraction < 0.5 as mixed). Produce spatial maps of key types (L2/3 IT, L5 PT, L6 CT, Astro, Oligo, Endo, etc.), a heatmap of mean fraction per anatomical cluster, and a dominant-type spatial map. Save `c2l_abundance_q05.tsv`, `c2l_fractions.tsv`, `c2l_cluster_by_celltype.tsv` to root_result; figures to root_figure.

steps.title: Link cell types to LIANA results
steps.description: Correlate per-spot cell-type abundance with the local LIANA bivariate LR scores (from visium_hne_liana_bivariate.h5ad), giving which LR co-localisation tracks which cell type. Also re-run li.mt.rank_aggregate with groupby = dominant type restricted to confident spots, as a cell-type-level view. Save `lr_vs_celltype_spearman.tsv`, a clustered heatmap figure, and `liana_dominant_celltype_results.tsv`.

steps.title: Write the notebook-ready script and report
steps.description: Write `squid04_cell2location.py` using your root_data/root_result/root_figure layout and the pdwritecsv helper. Write a short markdown summary of results and caveats (cortex-only reference, the N_cells prior, fractions not cell counts). Save both as artifacts.

desired_outputs: cell-type fraction tables and spatial maps

feasibility.rationale: Both datasets and methods are standard (this pairing is the squidpy/Tangram tutorial data). Main limitation: the reference covers cortex only, so neuronal fractions in thalamus, hypothalamus, striatum and hippocampus will be forced onto cortical neuron types; glial and vascular types are shared across the brain and remain interpretable. The cell2location spatial model trains on CPU (~30–60 min). Priors now follow the cell2location preprint in your studies folder.
